newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dlr ends steady after Brash's FEC appearance.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dlr ends steady after Brash's FEC appearance.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended Wednesday's session on a steady note with the market not drawing much from Reserve Bank governor Don Brash's comments to a parliamentary committee early in the session.
Brash told the powerful Finance and Expenditure Committee that the economy may have rebounded in the June quarter after a 0.5 percent decline in GDP over the March quarter.
The effect on the currency was minimal.
By 4.50 p.m. (0450 GMT) the Kiwi was at US$0.6782/89, little-changed from its 0.6785/91 opening, having traded a 0.6767-90 range on the day.
The Trade-Weighted Index fell to 66.56 from 66.87, which saw the Monetary Conditions Index go to 764.60 from 780.
The currency was looking slightly soft but the market would be wary of pushing it lower from here, said one dealer.
"I guess he (Brash) is happy with the easier conditions but I think it's a matter of 'boys, don't push it too far too fast'," the dealer said.
"There could be some room for interest rates to bounce back up to alleviate the downside pressure on the MCI at the moment but, for the time being, the Kiwi still looks a little soft," he said.
The Kiwi gained a little support from the Australian dollar's strength after news that Moody's was taking a positive outlook on Australia's credit rating.
But overnight, the Kiwi was not expected to venture far from a 0.6760-90 band.
